pages.title: Flexible glass storage
pages.text: Three tiers hold $(thing)30, 60 or 120 ordinary stacks$(). Any mix of items is allowed, with normal stack limits. All six faces support item insertion and extraction, including while locked.$(br2)The glass cube displays up to eight different floating items at a time. More plentiful items appear more often; previews fade and refresh about every five seconds.

pages.title: The inventory panel
pages.text: Right-click the cube to open its Storage panel. Stored stacks are above a separator; your main inventory and hotbar are below.$(br2)Hover over a side arrow to scroll the storage columns. Click to jump three columns, or hold left-click to scroll faster.$(br2)Beside Storage, $(thing)A-Z$() sorts item names and $(thing)Count$() sorts largest stacks first. Empty slots move to the end. Stacks keep their item data; your inventory is unchanged.

pages.title: Moving items
pages.text: $(li)Hold left-click on a stack, aim at the destination and release.$(li)Or click a source, then click the destination.$(li)Sneak-click transfers immediately to the other inventory.$(br2)Click the selected source again to cancel. Right-click the panel or use X to close. The ? button opens this manual entry. Items stay safely in their source until a move completes.

pages.title: Tier II: 60 stacks
pages.text: Each tier has its own populated Constructor blueprint; JEI lists the complete materials. Keep the blueprint in adjacent Blueprint Storage.$(br2)Tier II needs 4 Advanced Circuits, 24 Silicon, 24 Silver, 12 Platinum, 8 Lithium, 4 Ender Pearls, 2 Flux Capacitors and 8 Glass.

pages.title: Tier III: 120 stacks
pages.text: The largest cube is deliberately expensive: 12 Advanced Circuits, 64 Silicon, 64 Silver, 32 Platinum, 24 Lithium, 16 Ender Pearls, 8 Flux Capacitors and 16 Glass.$(br2)Breaking any tier preserves its stored items in the dropped cube. No flux is needed to store or transfer items.

pages.title: Locks and city access
pages.text: Nearby Locks and Wireless Locks can control unkeyed cubes of all three tiers. A cube with its own storage key cannot be overridden by an unrelated controller. Locking closes open panels and blocks player transfers, breaking and automation insertion and extraction.$(br2)Cubes placed in dungeon templates receive loot and the city’s storage lock as their section loads. Use that city’s storage-access Key Card to toggle the lock, as with its 2×2 Storage Cubes. The final AI Core drops the storage-access reward.
